angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 236,538 km at 9.10 pc = 0.35 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 109.8548 +/- 0.0259 mas (same row, RUWE 1.17): 9.10 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.34 solar radii from Morin et al., arXiv:0711.1418, Sect. 7: radius 0.34 solar radii (R sin i = 0.32 +/- 0.01, R ~ 0.34 for i ~ 70 deg (Sect. 7)) (https://arxiv.org/abs/0711.1418): 236,538 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.28 solar masses from Morin et al., arXiv:0711.1418, Sect. 7: mass 0.28 solar masses (0.28 +/- 0.05 from M_K (Sect. 7)) (https://arxiv.org/abs/0711.1418); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3240 K from TESS Input Catalog 8.2 (VizieR IV/39/tic82), TIC 283410775: Teff (https://vizier.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/VizieR?-source=IV/39/tic82). Spin inclination 70 degrees and rotation period 0.4456 d from Morin et al., arXiv:0711.1418, Sect. 7: rotation period 0.4456 d and an axis 70 degrees from the line of sight, the values its magnetic maps were made with (https://arxiv.org/abs/0711.1418). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
